posts.content:
Years ago, long before 6sense, I had one of those moments as a marketing leader that totally deflates you.  

Our pipeline numbers were incredible. I felt like we were crushing it. 

Included in that pipeline were three accounts that looked white-hot. All of them showed heavy buying signals and were in our ICP. Everything looked like the textbook definition of "ready to engage." 

I walked into my meeting with the sales team feeling great about what we had built. 

But then a rep asked, "Wait, why are we chasing these?" 

So I pulled up the data, showed him the signals, the research, the intent. 

He was completely unimpressed. "Yeah, but those accounts aren't going anywhere." 

Turns out, two of those three accounts were kicking tires because they were under budget pressure, not because they had a problem to solve. The third had a champion who was leaving in 30 days.  

How had we not caught that? Why were we so wrong? 

Turns out our signals were real. So was the research. What was missing was the context. 

The question has to go beyond, "Are they looking?"  

We have to ask:  

> Why are they looking?  
> What does that mean for how they'll buy?  
> Who has to believe in this before they take action? 

That’s the intelligence beneath the signals, and that’s what my team and I were missing. It’s what 6sense works obsessively to change. 

At Breakthrough 2026, we’ll show how we’re making sure the context shows up when and where it’s needed.  

Because no one wants that deflated “how did we get this so wrong?” feeling. We want to build pipeline we can trust and act on.

Are you Team “Long Live ABM” or Team “ABM Is Dead?”  

Either way, you’re probably right. 

The account-based approach continues to be the backbone of good marketing: focus on the right accounts, align marketing and sales around a shared ICP, and personalize based on buying stage and intent. 

The part that’s dying is the delivery model. 

GTM teams today are working across CRM, sales engagement, data warehouses, AI agents, workflows, and reporting environments. Intelligence that stays locked in one ABM platform is less useful than intelligence that travels to the moment where a decision gets made. 

That shift matters even more in the Agentic GTM era. 

AI agents can trigger outreach, route accounts, and personalize at scale. But if they’re acting on isolated signals without context, they can be very fast and very wrong. 

In my latest Forbes article, I wrote about why ABM as a methodology still matters, and what it looks like in the Agentic GTM era.

posts.content:
I’ve read that by the time our children turn 18, we’ve already spent about 90% of the time we’ll ever spend with them in our lifetime. I’m not sure if that’s exactly true, but standing at my son Vann’s high school graduation last Friday night, it certainly felt that way. 

I have this pit in my stomach that feels heavier every day. In four short weeks, Jim and I will leave one of our favorite people in the world in New Haven, CT, to start his college adventure. Then we will come home without him. 

Like every parent, I find myself asking the same questions. Did we teach him everything he needs to know? Did we do enough? Did we help shape the man he is becoming? Did we prepare him for what comes next?

The truth is, I don’t know the answer to that, but what I do know is that for 18 years, I’ve watched him show up every single day. I’ve watched him work when nobody was watching. He always says "Grind in private so you can shine in public." 

I’ve watched him choose discipline over excuses, commitment over comfort, and team over self. I’ve watched him get knocked down, get back up, and keep moving forward. I get choked up just watching him do life so intentionally.

Football and school taught him a lot of things, but the greatest lesson may be that WILL matters more than SKILL. Talent can open doors, but heart keeps you in the room. He used a quote in his college application essays from Kevin Durant that says, “Hard work beats talent when talent doesn’t work hard.” 

Effort compounds. Character travels. And the people who refuse to quit usually end up exactly where they’re supposed to be.

Over the last four years (shoot, 18 years!), I’ve watched hard work in the classroom and hard work on the field come together in a way that feels almost poetic. Not because the path was easy, but because he earned every step of it.

Today, I couldn’t be more proud. And if I’m honest, I couldn’t be more heartbroken.

Because while graduation is a celebration of everything that’s ahead for him, it’s also an acknowledgment that this chapter has ended. The late-night conversations because I refuse to go to bed until he is home, the Friday night lights, the rides to practice, the daily check-ins in the kitchen, the basic life lessons like "how do I address this thank you note" (because somehow they don't teach that in school anymore), and all the other moments that we take for granted...they all wove together to quietly become the fabric of our life. (And I love this life!)

What a privilege it has been to be your mom, Vann. The world is getting a remarkable young man.

And while I’m excited for everything waiting for you, I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t already counting the days until you come home.

posts.content:
Our team just published new research on how B2B GTM teams find, prioritize, and engage buyers in 2026. The headline isn't what you'd expect. 

It's not that AI has transformed how we go to market. It hasn't. What it has done is move into every organization without changing the underlying mental model driving the decisions. 

And that mental model is the problem. 

Most GTM teams are still built around the form fill, the MQL. In other words, they’re waiting for moment a buyer identifies themselves.  

What the research makes clear, and what buyers have been telling us for three years, is that by the time that happens, the decision is largely already made.  

A buying group of 10-plus people spent six months in silent research, built a shortlist, and landed on a preferred vendor before your BDR ever got the call. That preferred vendor wins the deal 8 out of 10 times. 

So when AI gets pointed at the form fill, it may automate outreach to individuals, score contacts, and optimize for the moment a buyer surfaces, but it does not solve the problem. It's just making the old mistake faster and with more confidence. 

The data backs this up. 97% of buying activity is anonymous, and yet only 42% of teams track anonymous signals at all.  

The signals most capable of identifying buyers during the Selection Phase (the part of the journey before consensus has formed, when influence is still possible) are the least used and the least trusted. 

Meanwhile, AI is applied across just two of five core GTM activities on average. Two thirds of teams are running it on rules humans defined, encoding the same contact-level assumptions into the technology meant to replace them.  

We haven't missed the window on getting this right, but the window won't stay open forever. 

Great job, as always, Kerry Cunningham and Sara Boostani (Frazier), M.S.

Every CMO I talk to right now is asking the same question. Not "are we targeting the right accounts," but the harder one: "Do we actually understand how buyers are moving right now?" 

Bruno Bertini, CMO of 8x8, brought that question to life at our company all-hands yesterday. I met Bruno a couple years ago when he was a 6sense customer, and I tried unsuccessfully to woo him to the competitor (my former employer). He never made the switch (which I really appreciate now), but the connection was made and a valuable friendship was born. 

His team has been on a multi-year journey with 6sense, moving from broad horizontal targeting to micro-vertical segmentation. Instead of just "automotive," for instance, they can target automotive dealers in the UK.  

That level of precision is what created the foundation for everything Bruno's go-to-market team is doing with AI now. 

AI is changing buyer behavior faster than most go-to-market teams are adapting. Traffic is shifting. Buyers are going to LLMs before they ever hit your website. The question Bruno is asking us to help answer: what does "in-market" even look like right now? 

That's the right question. And it's the one we're building toward. 

Thanks again for your time and insights, Bruno. Candid feedback in front of the whole company is the kind of partnership that truly makes us better.

posts.content:
Last-touch attribution answers a narrow question: What happened right before the meeting? 

It does not tell you what actually shaped the buying journey. 

Paid search, events, webinars, thought leadership, and brand often influence buyers long before they convert. A last-touch model can make those investments look ineffective. Worse, it can lead marketers to cut the very programs helping create demand. 

Multitouch attribution isn’t perfect, but it gives leaders a much more useful view of relative contribution across the full journey. 

In this conversation with The Future of Marketing Podcast, one of the many topics we covered was how moving beyond first- and last-touch attribution changed the way I evaluate performance, allocate budget, and decide what deserves more investment. 

Give it a listen and let me know what you think. Link to episode in comments.
